summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against every clause of the selected Latin working source. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the necessity of entering God's kingdom, the restricted assertion that none of this innocent kind will perish, the prompt return after wrongdoing, the ethical commands, and the shepherds' accountability and increased punishment for lying. Repentance fits the moral-spiritual context without added doctrinal conditions. The notes disclose the collective interpretation of the unusual spirit wording and the alternatives for dissipata/dissipati. They also distinguish editorially supplied [pro] from manuscript-preserved wording, consistently with the supplied apparatus report. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to this working source and disclosure of the supplied reports; it does not authenticate unseen images, certify editions, or establish exhaustive collation or a unique interpretation.
